text:
Elena (sales-ops): Quick heads-up — we've published a rate card update (v3.2) that consolidates SKUs and adds new commit tiers. Please review today if you have active POCs or outstanding LOIs.

DealBot: Rate card v3.2 uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.com/ratecards/v3.2.pdf :page_with_curl:

James O'Connor (AE): thanks. does this affect already-signed LOIs or only new SOWs?

Elena (sales-ops): only new SOWs and new commits by default. we can grandfather deals if sales requests it — pass to @Sarah Li with justification and term end date.

Priya Patel (Sales Eng): quick question on SKU consolidation — are embeddings and rerank bundled now or still separate line items?

Elena (sales-ops): embeddings + rerank are now a single 'vector-ops' SKU. price parity preserved at small commits; big commits get better blended discounts. see snippet:

```
commit_tiers:
  0-50k: 20% off
  50k-200k: 30% off
  200k+: 40% off
special_terms: [custom SLAs, private deploy add-ons]
```

Miguel Alvarez (Finance): discount caps? do we need finance approval beyond 40%? also what's the impact on ARR recognition modeling? :eyes: 

Elena (sales-ops): discount cap stays at 50% with escalations to finance+revops for anything >40%. ARR modeling: small change, finance will provide updated guidance by EOD.

Anika Rao (Legal): any new compliance/legal risk with SKU consolidation or special terms language? if we add 'private deploy add-ons' we should confirm data residency clauses. I'll review the redlines.

Sarah Li (Deal Desk): noted. For grandfathering requests, include: original SOW date, requested end date, reason, and a signed LOI if possible. I'll triage approvals — target SLA 48 hours.

James O'Connor (AE): can sales still request one-time credits or usage-contingent ramps under the new card?

Elena (sales-ops): one-time credits allowed but must be logged in the deal form and capped per-account. usage ramps allowed as short-term addendum (90 days). Both need SD approval if >$25k.

Priya Patel (Sales Eng): pinging @Miguel Alvarez for technical POC pricing guidance — any special quotas for heavy KV cache tests?

Miguel Alvarez (Finance): for POCs, use dev rate (50% of list) up to 30 days; anything longer we need a commit or loaner credit structure. I'll add a finance note to the doc.

DealBot: Reminder: Rate card changelog appended to Confluence page (v3.1 -> v3.2): https://confluence.redwood.com/ratecards/changelog

Elena (sales-ops): thanks all. if anyone spots issues in wording that will block enterprise legal or security reviews, escalate here with @Anika. planning to announce to customers tomorrow morning. :rocket:
